problem: Consider the parabola ${x}^{2}-8y=0.$ Given that $x=x(t),$ $y=y(t),$ and that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=\frac{1}{8}$ on the curve at the point $(4,2),$ find the value of  $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}$ at that point.
worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-8y & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}-8y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8y) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(8y) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2x)-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot 8 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=\frac{1}{8},$ $x=4,$ and $y=2,$ and solve $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2\cdot (4))-(\frac{1}{8})\cdot 8 & =0 \\ 8\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-1 & =0 \\ 8\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =1 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
